title: Desk Basis: Currency Presentation on the Payments Already Taken for a Vacation Package
content:
The figure taken now on a package among the Vacation Package Products carries a currency presentation loading, and the payments already standing on the package ledger decide it. The payments counted are the deposit lines and the instalment lines standing against the package, each carrying the currency the party was presented with. The operator's own currency is US dollars.

**Where every payment was presented in another currency.** Where every payment already taken on the package was presented in a currency other than the operator's own and at least one payment has been taken — that is, where no payment line shows US dollars and the count of payment lines is 1 or more — the loading is the whole of it increased by the product's conversion markup, that markup being the percentage published against the product booked.

**Where some but not all were.** Where some but not all of the payments already taken were presented in a currency other than the operator's own — that is, where at least 1 payment line shows US dollars and the count of such lines is fewer than the count of all payment lines — the loading is the whole of it increased by that markup taken at the part-presentation share published for this calculation, which is 50 per cent.

**Where none were.** Where every payment line already taken shows US dollars, or where no payment has yet been taken at all, no loading of this kind is added.

| Payment lines standing against the package | Of those, shown in US dollars | Loading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 or more | none | the whole of it increased by the product's conversion markup |
| 2 or more | at least 1, but fewer than all | the whole of it increased by that markup taken at 50 per cent |
| 1 or more | all of them | none of this kind |
| none | not applicable | none of this kind |

*Worked hypothetically.* A package on the Flex Bundle Package, a product publishing a conversion markup of 3.0 per cent, carries 3 payment lines. Where none of the three shows US dollars, a figure taken now of 1,000.00 USD is loaded to 1,030.00 USD. Where 1 of the three shows US dollars, the markup is taken at 50 per cent, giving 1.5 per cent, and the same figure is loaded to 1,015.00 USD.
